sub: Complete Guide: Concepts, Architecture, Configuration, Use Cases and Best Practices

Overview.p: A load balancer distributes incoming traffic across multiple servers (targets) for high availability, performance and scalability. It acts as a single entry point and sends requests only to healthy targets. The Application Load Balancer (ALB) works at Layer 7, so it understands HTTP and HTTPS.
Think of a hotel receptionist. Every guest comes to one desk. The receptionist checks which rooms are ready and sends each guest to the right one. If a room is under repair, nobody is sent there.

An e-commerce company launches a big sale. User traffic spreads across several web servers in different AZs. If one server becomes unhealthy, the ALB stops sending traffic to it and uses the healthy ones. Users never notice.

items: High availability: traffic spreads across AZs
Fault tolerance: unhealthy targets are skipped automatically
Horizontal scaling: add or remove servers easily
Health checks: only healthy targets get traffic
Path and host based routing: different apps behind one URL
HTTPS/TLS termination: handles certificates for you
Works with Security Groups and AWS WAF
Backend servers need not be public

Overview.p: Client → ALB → Listener → Rule → Target Group → Healthy Target

items: 👤 Client
🌐 Internet (DNS)
⚖ ALB Listener 80/443
📜 Listener Rule
🎯 Target Group
🔲 EC2 Target
📄 Response
Client sends a request to the ALB DNS name
ALB receives it on a listener (port 80 or 443)
Listener rules are checked by priority
Request goes to the target group (healthy targets only)
Target replies and the ALB returns the response to the client

Architecture.p: Place the ALB in at least 2 public subnets in different AZs. The ALB creates a node in each AZ. Targets can sit in private subnets. If one AZ fails, traffic continues through the other AZ.

Components.p: Stickiness keeps one user on the same target (cookie based). Weighted target groups send for example 90% to the old version and 10% to the new version, useful for blue-green and canary releases.

Examples.p: Many users hit the website during a sale. The ALB spreads them across web servers in two AZs. Auto Scaling adds servers when CPU is high and the ALB starts using them once they pass health checks.
One domain, many apps. /api/* goes to the API target group, /images/* to the image service, /admin/* to the admin servers. One ALB replaces three.
Create two target groups (v1 and v2). Send 90% to v1 and 10% to v2 using weights. If v2 is fine, move to 100%. If not, move back in seconds.
A small API can run on Lambda. Add the Lambda function as a target and the ALB calls it on each HTTP request. No servers to manage.

code: aws elbv2 create-target-group --name web-tg --protocol HTTP --port 80 --vpc-id vpc-0abc123 --target-type instance --health-check-path /health
aws elbv2 create-load-balancer --name web-alb --subnets subnet-111 subnet-222 --security-groups sg-0abc123

CLI Commands.p: Values like vpc-0abc123, subnet-111 and <tg-arn> are examples. Replace them with your real IDs and ARNs.

items: What is an ALB?
A Layer 7 load balancer that routes HTTP/HTTPS traffic to targets using rules and health checks.
Why use a target group?
It holds the backend targets and the health check settings. The ALB routes only to healthy targets in the group.
ALB vs NLB?
ALB understands HTTP (path/host routing, Layer 7). NLB is Layer 4, extremely fast and supports static IPs.
What is a health check?
A periodic request to each target (path, port, interval). Targets that fail are marked unhealthy and get no traffic.
How does path-based routing work?
A listener rule matches the URL path (e.g. /api/*) and forwards to a specific target group.
Where do you place an ALB?
In at least 2 public subnets in different AZs. Targets can be in private subnets.
How do you make an ALB secure?
HTTPS with ACM, HTTP to HTTPS redirect, security group chain (ALB to targets), WAF, access logs.
Why does the ALB show 502 or 503?
502: bad response from target. 503: no healthy targets. Check health check path, security groups and the app.
How does ALB work with Auto Scaling?
Attach the target group to the Auto Scaling Group. New instances register automatically and old ones are removed.
Client > ALB > Listener > Rule > Target Group > Healthy Target
ALB is the entry point (not the server)
A listener listens on one port
Rules decide where to send
A target group can hold many targets
Only healthy targets receive traffic
